From 361e0ff456a8daf9753c18030533256e4133ce7a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alice Ryhl <aliceryhl@google.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2025 11:24:24 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] rust_binder: remove spin_lock() in rust_shrink_free_page()

When forward-porting Rust Binder to 6.18, I neglected to take commit
fb56fdf8b9a2 ("mm/list_lru: split the lock to per-cgroup scope") into
account, and apparently I did not end up running the shrinker callback
when I sanity tested the driver before submission. This leads to crashes
like the following:

	============================================
	WARNING: possible recursive locking detected
	6.18.0-mainline-maybe-dirty #1 Tainted: G          IO
	
diff --git a/drivers/android/binder/page_range.rs b/drivers/android/binder/page_range.rs
index 9379038f61f5..fdd97112ef5c 100644
--- a/drivers/android/binder/page_range.rs
+++ b/drivers/android/binder/page_range.rs
@@ -727,8 +727,5 @@ fn drop(self: Pin<&mut Self>) {
     drop(mm);
     drop(page);
 
-    // SAFETY: We just unlocked the lru lock, but it should be locked when we return.
-    unsafe { bindings::spin_lock(&raw mut (*lru).lock) };
-
     LRU_REMOVED_ENTRY
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch removes an unnecessary `spin_lock()` call in `rust_shrink_free_page()` within `drivers/android/binder/page_range.rs`. This lock acquisition became incorrect after the Linux 6.18 kernel changed `list_lru` locking to per‑cgroup scope (commit `fb56fdf8b9a2`), causing a recursive locking warning. The fix eliminates the re‑locking of the LRU lock, which was already unlocked at that point, thereby preventing the reported `WARNING: possible recursive locking detected`.

Here is the commit message:
rust_binder: remove spin_lock() in rust_shrink_free_page()

When forward-porting Rust Binder to 6.18, I neglected to take commit
fb56fdf8b9a2 ("mm/list_lru: split the lock to per-cgroup scope") into
account, and apparently I did not end up running the shrinker callback
when I sanity tested the driver before submission. This leads to crashes
like the following:

	============================================
	WARNING: possible recursive locking detected
	6.18.0-mainline-maybe-dirty #1 Tainted: G          IO
	--------------------------------------------
	kswapd0/68 is trying to acquire lock:
	ffff956000fa18b0 (&l->lock){+.+.}-{2:2}, at: lock_list_lru_of_memcg+0x128/0x230

	but task is already holding lock:
	ffff956000fa18b0 (&l->lock){+.+.}-{2:2}, at: rust_helper_spin_lock+0xd/0x20

	other info that might help us debug this:
	 Possible unsafe locking scenario:

	       CPU0
	       ----
	  lock(&l->lock);
	  lock(&l->lock);

	 *** DEADLOCK ***

	 May be due to missing lock nesting notation

	3 locks held by kswapd0/68:
	 #0: ffffffff90d2e260 (fs_reclaim){+.+.}-{0:0}, at: kswapd+0x597/0x1160
	 #1: ffff956000fa18b0 (&l->lock){+.+.}-{2:2}, at: rust_helper_spin_lock+0xd/0x20
	 #2: ffffffff90cf3680 (rcu_read_lock){....}-{1:2}, at: lock_list_lru_of_memcg+0x2d/0x230

To fix this, remove the spin_lock() call from rust_shrink_free_page().

Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Fixes: eafedbc7c050 ("rust_binder: add Rust Binder driver")
Signed-off-by: Alice Ryhl <aliceryhl@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251202-binder-shrink-unspin-v1-1-263efb9ad625@google.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

split the lock to per-cgroup scope"). The old code attempted to re-lock the LRU lock after the shrinker callback had already released it, but due to the change to per-cgroup locking, this caused a recursive locking warning.

-    // SAFETY: We just unlocked the lru lock, but it should be locked when we return.
-    unsafe { bindings::spin_lock(&raw mut (*lru).lock) };
-

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```rust
unsafe { bindings::spin_lock(&raw mut (*lru).lock) };
```
Reason:  
After the LRU lock was split into per-cgroup locks (commit fb56fdf8b9a2), the shrinker callback `rust_shrink_free_page` already holds the lock via the list_lru API. The explicit `spin_lock()` call attempts to acquire the same lock again, causing a recursive locking deadlock warning.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```rust
// The line `unsafe { bindings::spin_lock(&raw mut (*lru).lock) };` is removed.
```
Reason:  
Removing the redundant `spin_lock()` avoids the double‑lock attempt. The lock is correctly managed by the list_lru shrinker infrastructure, so no explicit locking is needed in the callback.
